claim_en: מחויאל ("Mechuyael") — first mention: soft yod, FULL with vav BEFORE the yod (Ramah's spelling rule for the first token).

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 4:18 (Masorah at Behaalotcha)
claim_en: ומחייאל ("and Mechiyael") — the SAME MAN respelled inside the SAME VERSE: first token vav, second token double yod — one of the Masorah's SEVEN CHANGING PAIRS (two spellings of one name in one context). The frozen unit held this letter-fact unattributed; the chain owns it.

וצלה גם הוא ("and Tzillah, she also") — הוא WRITTEN with vav (the masculine skeleton), READ as feminine: SNAPSHOT points it הִוא with hiriq (the read-form's vowel inside the written form) — the Torah's standing written-vs-read (ktiv/qere) on this pronoun, confirmed here by manuscripts and the early print (Minchat Shai).
וצלה גם הוא — the gimel of גם ("also") is SOFT (no dagesh, the doubling dot): gimel+patach contiguous in SNAPSHOT.

ולשת גם הוא ("and to Seth, he also") — the same phrase four verses on, and THIS gimel carries the dagesh (doubling dot): Tzillah's soft גם and Seth's hard גם are a pointed minimal pair across the chapter's pivot.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 4:22 (Western vs Eastern Masorah)
claim_en: תובל קין ("Tubal-Cain") — the Easterners write and read it as ONE word; the Westerners, "and we hold like the Westerners" (Minchat Shai, Ramah), as TWO. SNAPSHOT: two tokens, תובל adjacent to קין, both occurrences.

תובל written FULL with vav — the Ramah: "in the Torah we find no plene ones besides these two" (both in this verse; Japheth's תבל, Gen 10:2, is defective). SNAPSHOT: exactly two plene tokens, both at 4:22.

האזנה ("give ear," the sword-song's summons) — the copies split: many point the zayin with segol; Chizkuni and old manuscripts with TSERE ("on the pattern of הפקדנה," the Mikhlol), the alef quiescent. SNAPSHOT: alef with silent sheva, zayin with TSERE — the Chizkuni camp.

The build-and-name operator of our 4:17 is read as the wicked man's bid for immortality - naming a city after a son so the name endures - answered by 'their inward thought is that their houses shall continue forever', and by the ruling that in the end 'their houses become their graves'.

check.note: A motive assigned to a build operator.

claim_en: THE GENEALOGY READ AS A SENTENCE-LEDGER. The line-names of our 4:18 are parsed as decree-verbs spoken against the line: Irad, 'I will expel them'; Mechuyael, 'I will erase them'; Metushael, 'I will uproot them'; and of Lemekh, 'what have I to do with Lemekh'. The register the machine reads as descent is read by the chain as a running judgment. The two-wives institution of the era is described beside it - one wife for offspring, one kept barren for company - and the seats REVERSE the roles of the two wives against one another, a variance carried dual-track.

check.note: A genealogy operator re-read as a judgment ledger, with a recorded role-reversal between seats.

claim_en: The craft-founder operators of our 4:20-22 are read darkly: the herdsman's holdings as provocation, the musician's instruments as serving idols, and the smith Tuval-Cain as the one who 'SEASONED Cain's transgression - Cain killed without an instrument; this one forges every cutting edge'. The first metallurgy operator is read as the origin of the weapons trade, joined back to the undecided weapon of the first murder.

check.note: A craft-install operator read as the origin of an industry, linked to the prior block's weapon dispute.

claim_en: A NAMED INFERENCE-FAILURE, GRADED AT A PRIMARY SEAT AND CANONIZED ANYWAY. Lemekh argues at our 4:24 from Cain's seven generations to his own seventy-seven - a light-and-heavy inference. Rebbi GRADES IT AND FAILS IT: 'a flawed a-fortiori, an a-fortiori of darkness - from whom would He ever collect His note?'. Yet the Jerusalem Talmud cites this very verse as the exhibit a-fortiori that one may not deny, with the editor's own note that the argument violates the form's rules and stands regardless. The corpus therefore records a middah applied WRONGLY and preserved as canonical text - the machine must carry the inference as recorded-and-failed, not as sound.

check.note: An inference rule explicitly graded as invalid at a primary seat while the verse carrying it stays canonical. The middah is recorded as attempted, not as licensed.

claim_en: The Seth install at our 4:25 is sighted FORWARD: 'she looked at that offspring who comes from ANOTHER PLACE - the messianic king', so the line the machine records as a replacement is read as a root. And the image-line is CUT at Enosh: 'Adam, Seth, Enosh - then silence: until here in the image and likeness; from here on the generations corrupted' - which sets the boundary the next unit's likeness-recap will re-open.

check.note: A forward reference on an install operator, and a boundary the following unit inherits.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 23:7; Mekhilta DeRabbi Yishmael, Tractate Bachodesh 6:9
claim_en: הוּחַל (huchal) at our 4:26 is read not as 'began to call' but as REBELLION - the profaning of the Name - and R. Simon censuses three places where the verb carries that sense: our 4:26, Genesis 6:1, and Nimrod's beginning. Verified at derivation: our 4:26 is the ONLY token of this form in the whole Torah, and it is the only PASSIVE (hophal) member of the group - the other two seats write the active form. The ocean's riposte is recorded with it: 'you called your names divine - I will call the sea's waters by My name', and the inundation's measure varies by seat, one giving geographic bounds and the tannaitic seat a third of the world.
